**Does corn pudding exist?**  
Yes. It is a documented Thanksgiving side dish, with recipes and references from sources such as [Martha Stewart](https://www.marthastewart.com/1155558/corn-pudding-chives) and the USDA’s [America’s Harvest](https://fns-prod.azureedge.us/americasharvest/founding/sides/corn-pudding).

**Is it common everywhere?**  
No evidence from these sources establishes that. The search describes it as served at Thanksgiving in **some regions and households**, so “regional or family-specific” is safer than “universal.” It may be familiar in parts of the American South and in individual family traditions, but prevalence varies.

**Was it documented at the 1621 harvest gathering?**  
Not as modern corn pudding. The source specifically cautions against projecting today’s dish onto the 1621 menu merely because corn was present. Corn at the gathering does **not** document a pudding made in the modern Thanksgiving sense.

So: **real dish, genuine Thanksgiving tradition for some families, but not an everywhere-American staple—and not documented as part of the 1621 meal.** The cited history search is curated and does not measure household prevalence.

In other words: they exist, and they may be familiar to people who follow food media, but there’s no evidence here that they’re broadly customary family staples. Viral reach is not the same as Aunt Linda’s annual recipe.
